subject: When can a sample become infinite?

messages.author: fb1667ba74f25458
messages.subject: When can a sample become infinite?
parts:
Hi all,
first, I love Stan, it is a great tool and I am very happy I started learning. Now, I am developing my first complex model in Stan (over RStan) and I noticed one peculiarity. I have a parameter with a lower bound and lognormal distribution:
parameters {
  int num_targets;
  vector<lower = 0>[num_targets] degradation;
  //lots of other stuff
}

model {
  //lots of other stuff
  vector[num_targets] log_d = log(degradation);
  target += normal_lpdf(log_d | -0.5,2);
  target += -log_d
  //lots of other stuff
}


Some of my computations provided infinite or nan values for distribution moments. After digging in I realized, that the source of the problem is that some elements of degradation may become infinite. I *think* it is related to the fact that my testing data is currently small and the model is not identifiable, I however want to understand this better. When can a model parameter be sampled as inf? Is this because the gradient from a previous step was infinite? Or are there other possible causes?

I tried running with test_grad = TRUE, but that crashes the R session :-(

Also, if I do not handle the nan/inf values in the model block, stan crashes the R session if compiled with -O3, but does not crash with -O1 -g is that expected or is it a bug? Any debugging hints will be greatly appreciated :-)

Thanks a lot.
Martin Cerny

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] When can a sample become infinite?
parts:
The problem is that double-precision floating point isn't very
precise. For example, if you have

real x;

real y = exp(x);

then if x > 400, y will be infinite.

So when gradients are infinite, it's usually an issue with
overflow. Or underflow and then a log if it's negative.

When you say infinite moments, you mean the posterior mean
as you get from printing?

There's a discussion in the manual of problematic posteriors,
and you can see that some kinds of additive non-identifiability
lead to improper posteriors---they have a ridge of constant
density running out to infinity.

- Bob

messages.author: fb1667ba74f25458
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] When can a sample become infinite?
parts:
Thanks, for the explanation, it points out some issues I have not considered.

I was probably a bit unclear about the error message I get. The message is 
normal_log: Location parameter is inf, but must be finite!

For staments similar to
y ~ normal(degradation, sigma)

But I do not think the distinction is important. Instead I would like to make my question a bit more precise:

Is there any other reason a sample can be infinite than
previous_value + gradient * step_size is infinite?


Thanks
Martin
